data.name: Whatsnew_1_1_0
data.value: • MC Server Launcher now runs on Linux too (not just Windows), thanks to a new cross-platform interface. • On Linux, download it as an AppImage from the releases; on Windows everything stays the same (installer and auto-update). • All 5 languages, the console, the players view and the visual configuration are kept.

data.name: Whatsnew_1_2_0
data.value: • You can now create Forge and Paper servers, on top of Vanilla and Fabric. • Built-in mods & plugins browser (Modrinth), filtered by your server's type and version, with sorting and one-click install. • Enable/disable or delete what's installed, and convert an existing server to another type while keeping the world. • Each server now shows a type badge.

data.name: Whatsnew_1_2_1
data.value: • More security: the Playit API key is now stored encrypted (previously plain text), on every OS. Migration is automatic. • Refreshed high-resolution app icon.

data.name: Whatsnew_1_2_2
data.value: • More security: Minecraft (Mojang), Java (Adoptium) and Paper downloads are now verified against their official checksum; a mismatch deletes the file and warns instead of using it.

data.name: Whatsnew_1_2_3
data.value: • More security: mods and plugins you install from Modrinth are now also verified against their official checksum before use.

data.name: Whatsnew_1_2_4
data.value: • More security: the Forge installer is now verified against Forge's own maven checksum, and the app's own updater checks the downloaded installer before running it.

data.name: Whatsnew_1_2_5
data.value: • If a server exits unexpectedly on its own (not via the Stop button), it's now restarted automatically (up to 3 attempts), showing the reason if a crash report is available. • Each server's console is now also saved to a persistent log file, so you don't lose the history when you close the app.

data.name: Whatsnew_1_3_0
data.value: • Automatic world backups: a zip is created before every start and when you stop the server, with configurable retention (the last 5, by default). • New "Backups" tab: make a manual backup anytime and restore any saved one with one click.

data.name: Whatsnew_1_4_0
data.value: • The app now minimizes to the system tray and notifies you when a player joins, the server crashes or the automatic restart gives up. • New search filter in the console and mini CPU/RAM charts in the status cards.

data.name: Whatsnew_1_12_1
data.value: • The console is no longer a grey wall. Each line is painted for what it is: errors red, warnings amber, player chat and joins/leaves in their own colours, and what the app says told apart from what the server says — they used to be mixed together with no way to know who was talking. • And it can be filtered by category, with a switch for each. Every switch carries its count, so “Errors 3” is visible without pressing anything; and if an error arrives while that category is off, the switch says so. • What you search for is marked inside the line, not just used to filter lines. In a long exception trace, that is the difference between finding it and seeing it. • Errors the server writes to its error stream now count as errors. They used to be mixed in with the rest of the output one line before they could be told apart. • The two new colours — chat and players — are editable in Settings. Error, warning and app take the ones you already chose for notifications, so red means the same thing everywhere in the app. • Fixed the colour labels in Settings being drawn on top of the swatches.

data.name: Whatsnew_1_12_0
data.value: • Notifications can now be told apart without reading them: each carries a colour for what happened and its own emoji. Green when somebody joins, amber when the server stops itself for being empty, red when it crashes. • The emoji is not decoration: colour alone does not reach anybody who cannot separate red from green, and shape does. • The four colours are editable in Settings, and the test button now shows all four at once so they can be compared. • Before starting, every mod and plugin is checked for what it needs. If something is missing you are told when you press Start — not on a tab nobody opens — with what is missing and which mod needs it, and you can install and start, start anyway, or cancel. • The check reads the jars themselves, so it works offline and does not depend on the store having its dependency list right. It now also understands Paper and Purpur plugins and Forge and NeoForge mods, which were previously invisible. • An automatic restart or a wake-on-demand never stops to ask: there is nobody there to answer.

data.name: Whatsnew_1_11_2
data.value: • The Bedrock port now shows from the first moment. The whole panel used to stay hidden until a tunnel lookup succeeded, so three different situations looked the same: a blank gap. • And it now says which state it is in: waiting for Playit to publish the address, no tunnel (local network only), ready, or could not be looked up. • Fixed crossplay being left half-enabled for ever: if a download failed, the setting stayed off internally and the address never appeared again, not even after restarting the app. • New servers no longer take a port a tunnel on your Playit account was already using. The search only looked at your own machine, and creating a tunnel there silently adopted the other one: two servers advertising a single address. • If a tunnel that is not this server's is there anyway, another port is chosen and it is said in the console, instead of keeping somebody else's. • Also: deleting a server now deletes its Bedrock tunnel even when its server.properties cannot be read — it used to be left orphaned, and its port handed to the next server as free.

data.name: Whatsnew_1_11_1
data.value: • Fixed a bug that broke crossplay in 1.11.0: writing the port Geyser advertises left the key indented two spaces too far, which made the config file invalid. It corrects itself at start-up. • And it was written every thirty seconds whether or not anything had changed, so the bug reached the disk with nobody touching anything. It is now written only when it really changes, and in a way a power cut cannot leave half done. • Five downloads used the file name the API gives without checking that it stayed inside the server's folder. They all go through the same check now. • Deleting a crossplay server looked its tunnel up by port number alone: if another tunnel on your account shared that number on the other protocol, the wrong one was deleted. The protocol is part of the match now. • Setting crossplay up on two stopped servers gave both the same Bedrock port, and the second Geyser failed to start. The other servers' ports are taken into account now. • Also: Minecraft versions written as “1.21.x” or “>= 1.21” are understood properly, and the Mods tab stops reading every file in the folder twice per install.

data.name: Whatsnew_1_11_0
data.value: • Installing a mod now brings the libraries it needs. That was what was missing when Fabric refused to start with “needs fabric-api, which you do not have”: they are resolved on Modrinth, dependencies of dependencies included, and installed in the same click. • Only the required ones, and never a second copy of something already there, because two copies of one mod break start-up just as thoroughly as none. • For servers you already had, the check-for-updates button now also says which libraries are missing and offers to install them. • Crossplay now says how far it gets on each type: it works on Paper, Purpur and Fabric; on NeoForge it connects and from there depends on the mods, which the card warns about in amber; on Vanilla and Forge there is no Geyser. • And with this, playing across platforms leaves beta.

data.name: Whatsnew_1_10_3_4
data.value: • WARNING: this is still a BETA. • Fixed a bug of mine that broke crossplay: the app left Geyser's authentication on “online” instead of “floodgate”, which is why “Someone tried to connect as a Java player!” appeared. It is written now, and corrected on servers that already existed, at start-up. • It was also writing a “remote:” section that Geyser 2.11 no longer reads — it renamed it to “java:” — and Floodgate's key is now pointed at where it actually is. • Folder names are properly checked: characters Windows forbids (silently removed before, leaving you with a different folder), reserved names like CON or COM1, and trailing dots or spaces. The parent folder is checked too. • The characters that stop Paper are still just “+” and “!”: I checked by starting a real Paper server in twenty-one differently named folders. Not #, not &, not %, not accents, not parentheses — so none of those are banned.

data.name: Whatsnew_1_10_3_3
data.value: • WARNING: this is still a BETA. • Bedrock can now see mod content, on Fabric: a new checkbox installs Hydraulic and Fabric API, and the blocks and items the mods add are converted for Bedrock clients. • On NeoForge it cannot, and the app now says exactly why: Hydraulic stopped publishing NeoForge builds in February 2026 and its module is still out of the build. For mods and Bedrock together, Fabric is today's route. • Paper no longer burns three retries on a failure it cannot change: if the folder has a “+” or a “!”, it is checked before starting and you are offered a rename, keeping the server and its world. • When the character sits in a folder above, no rename is offered — that would move everything else under it too; it is explained and left to you.

data.name: Whatsnew_1_10_3_2
data.value: • WARNING: this is still a BETA. • The server type is properly fixed now: the picker was one selection behind. On clicking a card, everything reacting to the change still read the previous type — which is why the first change appeared to do nothing and the second one worked. • Paper and Purpur will not start when the folder path contains a “+” or a “!”. You are now warned while typing the name, stopped from creating or converting there, and if it happens anyway the app explains it instead of silently retrying three times. • Mod-loader servers have no such limitation — which is why a folder that had worked for months stopped working the moment it became Paper.

data.name: Whatsnew_1_10_3_1
data.value: • WARNING: this is still a BETA. From now on betas carry a fourth number (1.10.3.1) to tell them apart from stable releases. • Fixed: changing a server's type from the edit window left the Bedrock and other-versions checkboxes holding the previous type's answer. You converted a Vanilla server to Paper and they still said Vanilla takes no plugins, as if the change had not happened. • When switching between a mod server and a plugin server, whatever was installed is moved to a dated folder of its own. The new type does not read it, and it used to sit there showing up in the list as though it still worked. Nothing is deleted: convert back and it is still there.

data.name: Whatsnew_1_10_3
data.value: • WARNING: this is still a BETA. • Picking the server type is no longer a list of names: it is a grid of cards saying which take plugins, which take mods, and which can be joined from Bedrock. • New type: Purpur. It is Paper with more settings, and it runs exactly the same plugins. • New checkbox for joining from other Minecraft versions: installs ViaVersion and ViaBackwards, for clients both newer and older than the server. • Fixed: turning crossplay on from the edit window saved the checkbox but installed nothing. • Fixed: the change-type window always opened on Fabric, which made the destructive conversion the default. It now opens on the type the server already is.

data.name: Whatsnew_1_10_2
data.value: • WARNING: this is still a BETA. • Fixed: when creating a server with Bedrock, Geyser and Floodgate now show up in the mods tab without pressing refresh. • New warning on Fabric and NeoForge: players joining from Bedrock arrive as a client with no mods, so mods adding blocks or items shut them out. It is said when you tick the box now, not once you can no longer get in. • And if it happens anyway, the app recognises the rejection in the console and explains it, instead of leaving you the English message telling you to install NeoForge on your phone. • To have both content and Bedrock players, the way is Paper with plugins.

data.name: Whatsnew_1_10_1
data.value: • WARNING: this is a BETA. Its main feature could not be tested end to end, because that needs joining from a real phone or console. • New: people can join the server from Bedrock too (phone, console, Windows 10/11). Turn it on with a checkbox when creating or editing a server. • The app installs Geyser and Floodgate, picks the port, creates the second tunnel and sets the port to advertise by itself — the part almost nobody gets right by hand. • Works on Paper, Fabric and NeoForge. On Forge and Vanilla the checkbox is greyed out and tells you why: Geyser publishes no build for them. • Note about Floodgate: players joining from Bedrock don't need a Java account, their identity isn't verified by Mojang, and their name shows with a dot in front. The whitelist accepts them all the same. • The update banner now tells betas apart, and says so before you press Update.

data.name: Whatsnew_1_10_0
data.value: • You can now create and manage NeoForge servers, or convert one you already have while keeping the world. The mod store filters itself by NeoForge. • For the Minecraft versions where NeoForge only ever published a beta, the app uses it and tells you before installing, not after. • The NeoForge installer is verified with SHA-256, stronger than the SHA-1 that is all Forge offers. No checksum, no install. • The idle-shutdown countdown, alerts for stopping and starting by itself, and the app no longer opening twice. • Fixed on Linux: minimizing to the tray left the window in the taskbar and brought it back empty. • The sleeping-server notice has its own colour in the server list, and updating no longer rearranges your desktop icons.

data.name: Whatsnew_1_9_2
data.value: • The countdown to the automatic shutdown is now shown in the window: you can see how long an empty server has left without doing the maths. • Two new optional alerts: when an empty server stops itself, and when one starts itself because somebody tried to join. • The app no longer opens twice. Launching it again brings back the window you already had, instead of a second copy that could not see what the first one was doing. • Fixed on Linux: minimizing to the tray left the app in the taskbar and brought it back as an empty window with no content. • The "server is off" notice now has its own colour in the server list, instead of inheriting whatever colour your MOTD ended on. • Updating no longer rearranges your desktop icons: the installer leaves the shortcut you already had where it was.

data.name: Whatsnew_1_9_1
data.value: • Your server can look after itself: it stops once nobody has been on for a while, and starts again as soon as someone tries to join. Turn it on in each server's settings. • Anyone trying to join while it is off gets a proper message, both in the server list and when pressing Join, instead of the usual connection error. • The app icon is no longer blurry on Linux and macOS: the smallest size was being packaged, scaled up.

data.name: Whatsnew_1_9_0
data.value: • Linux and macOS now update themselves, just like Windows: the Update button downloads, verifies and installs the new version and reopens the app, instead of sending you to the page to do it by hand. • New button in Settings to add the app to your desktop, icon and all. • The mod store no longer gets stuck on old data after a one-off network failure, and the app uses less CPU on Linux when you don't use Playit.

data.name: Whatsnew_1_8_2
data.value: • Your Playit key is no longer exposed: it used to travel on the agent's command line, where any process on the machine could read it. It is now handed over in a private file that is deleted when the agent stops. • The Java the app downloads is never installed unverified: if Adoptium doesn't provide its checksum, the install is cancelled instead of running something unchecked. • The "an update is available" link now goes through the same validation as every other link in the app.

data.name: Whatsnew_1_8_1
data.value: • A download cut off halfway no longer destroys the file you already had: mods, servers and Java are fetched to one side and only replace the working file once complete and verified. • Mod install errors are now visible: a checksum that doesn't match, a dropped connection or a running server is reported on screen instead of failing silently. • Fixed the system tray preferences: they no longer fall back to their defaults when the app restarts.

data.name: Whatsnew_1_8_0
data.value: • The mod store now has a full details page: description in your language, gallery, versions, dependencies, links and related mods, without leaving the app. • New Filters panel: pick several categories at once, see which ones are applied and remove them one by one. Changing a filter takes the list back to the top. • Every mod comes with a plain-language summary of what it does, and warns you when it also has to be installed on the client.

data.name: Whatsnew_1_7_3
data.value: • You now choose in Settings what the window buttons do: whether minimizing sends the app to the tray (leaving the taskbar), and whether the X quits the app or also sends it to the tray. • Keep it like 1.7.2 or get the previous behavior back, without restarting the app.

data.name: Whatsnew_1_7_2
data.value: • Minimizing now sends the app to the system tray: it leaves the taskbar and lives on as the icon next to the clock (servers keep running). • The close (X) button really quits the app again, like it used to. • To bring the window back, click the tray icon.

data.name: Whatsnew_1_7_1
data.value: • Playit is safer: the official agent downloaded by the app is verified against a pinned SHA-256 before it runs, including cached copies. • The Playit connection proxy now rejects traffic outside the expected flow, rate-limits attempts per IP, and uses the same agent version the app downloads. • Death notifications avoid more false positives, and per-server notification preferences are copied independently.

data.name: Whatsnew_1_7_0
data.value: • Configurable notifications: choose by type (player joins/leaves, deaths and PvP kills, server crash, auto-restart gave up), with a master switch and per-server overrides. Each alert says which server it's from, and there's a button to preview how they look. • New Settings button that gathers language and notifications in one place. • Playit made much easier: connect your account by pasting a code (no keys or files) from Settings or when creating a tunnel; the app creates and manages the tunnel for you.

data.name: Whatsnew_1_6_3
data.value: • Lower background usage: with the app in the tray, status polling runs at a tenth of its usual rate (everything returns to normal when you open the window). • With several servers, the Playit tunnel lookup is done once and shared instead of repeated per server. • The console handles very verbose servers (e.g. Forge booting) with far less UI work, and the on-disk log is written in batches. • Internal cleanup: fewer repeated settings reads and unified duplicated code.

data.name: Whatsnew_1_6_2
data.value: • Security: the Forge installer now requires its checksum and its structure is validated before it runs; the Fabric jar was already validated since 1.6.1. • The Playit key is never saved unencrypted: if encryption ever fails, it isn't saved and you're warned. • The settings editor and the MOTD can no longer sneak extra lines into server.properties. • Player names are validated against Minecraft's real pattern before sending commands. • Freeing a busy port re-checks the process is still the same one before closing it, and mod icons have size and type limits.

data.name: Whatsnew_1_6_1
data.value: • Reliability: the server list is saved atomically with a backup copy; if the file gets damaged, it recovers on its own and lets you know. • Restarting a hung server no longer silently "does nothing", and the world backup on stop waits until the process is fully gone. • Modern Forge servers also check and install the right Java before starting. • Security: the in-app update requires verifying the installer (checksum) before running it, and the downloaded Fabric jar is validated before use. • Details: installing a loader and then cancelling the edit no longer desyncs the server type; the player counter can't be spoofed from chat; default RAM unified (2/4 GB).

data.name: Tun_Empty
data.value: Your Playit account has no tunnels open.

data.name: Tun_NotConnected
data.value: Connect your Playit account in Settings to see your tunnels.

data.name: Tun_OrphanHint
data.value: Left over from a server that no longer exists. It uses up a slot on your account and serves nothing.

data.name: Tun_ClashHint
data.value: Another tunnel points at the same local port. Only one of them can work.

data.name: Tun_DeleteFmt
data.value: Delete the tunnel "{0}"? This does not touch any server.

data.name: Ping_Fine
data.value: All normal. If it's bad for someone, it's their connection.

data.name: Ping_ServerSlow
data.value: It's your server: it's slow to answer right here.

data.name: Ping_TunnelSlow
data.value: Your server is fine. What's slow is the Playit tunnel.

data.name: Ping_TunnelDown
data.value: Your server answers here, but nothing answers through the tunnel.

data.name: Ping_Disclaimer
data.value: Both start and end at this computer. This is NOT your friends' ping: the stretch between them and Playit never touches this machine and cannot be measured.

data.name: Tun_RenameHint
data.value: The name is just for you: you see it here and on playit.gg, and it changes neither the address nor the port.

data.name: Addr_Share
data.value: Copy address and port to share
